title: nothing published in 14d was accepted: 22 measured post(s), 0 like(s), 0 comment(s), 0 save(s)
evidence: 25 post(s) published in the last 14d, 22 with insights collected; totals over the measured set: likes=0 comments=0 saves=0 reach=71 (mean reach 3.2/post). The harness is producing normally -- renders complete, posts land, the queue holds at target -- so every machine-level check stays green while the RESULT is zero. This is the acceptance counter for the 2026-09-28 GO/PIVOT/KILL gate; a flat engagement read there is this condition, not a starved pipeline. Account reach attribution, newest measured snapshot (09-24 14:22): non-follower=0 follower=5 total=5. Instagram's account insights answer `reach` with `breakdown=follow_type`, so this is the platform's own split, not an inference from a per-post sum: non-follower=0 means nothing outside the follower list was shown these posts at all -- a DISTRIBUTION ceiling rather than a content problem, and the lever the gate's pivot candidate names. Independent witness: Instagram's own account-level counter (accounts_engaged, period=day) read 0 across 4 measured day(s) in this window, so the zero is stated by the platform rather than produced by our collection. Self-closes when a published post is engaged with (any like/comment/save in the window) -- that predicate stays on the per-post columns the gate reads, so a platform counter that disagrees is reported here and never closes it silently.

notes.note: 2026-09-24 08:2xZ ops-triage: no change to the condition (0 like/comment/save on the measured set), and no decision inside the experiment -- the pre-registered read at 10-05 still owns it. This pass closed a MONITORING gap that sat directly under this item's own premise (the hashtags are 'the account's only discoverability lever at 157 followers'): nothing measured whether that lever actually SHIPPED. The tags are appended to a local variable at send time (packs/scheduling/lib/tasks/scheduled_posting.rake: published_caption = post.caption + Array(post.hashtags).join(' ')) and never persisted, so scheduling_posts.caption does NOT contain them and the local DB cannot tell a tagged send from an untagged one -- the same blind spot under which all 197 posted items shipped with zero tags for the account's whole life. FIX (this commit): new probe check check_published_hashtags_shipped + pure hashtag_shipped_verdict reads the PUBLISHED CAPTION BACK FROM INSTAGRAM (media node field caption) and counts the column's tags inside it; an unreadable media is UNKNOWN (never a failure) and only a caption containing NONE of a non-empty column's tags fires. VERIFIED with ground truth, not bookkeeping: readback on posts 331/323/339/330 -> column_tags=10 shipped_tags=10 for each (the caption tail carries all ten, e.g. '#lifestyleblogger ... #tinyjoys'). The check is not vacuous: the identical rails script with each column tag mangled ('#food' -> '#foodzz') returned shipped_tags=0 for the same three posts and hashtag_shipped_verdict fired warn naming ids 331/323/339; healthy path returns None. selftest 625 assertions 0 failures (was 614); checks-audit 56 checks 2 firing 0 raised 0 unreadable (was 55). Also verified this pass, and NOT a defect: the producer is pillar-targeted now -- future queue rows carry #food #cooking #dining / #fashion #style / #travel #adventure according to photo.content_pillar, with the constant brand-tag set confined to 3 pre-fix rows (posts 324/332/333, created 09-17, publishing 09-25/09-26) that QueuedHashtagBackfill will not rewrite by design (it fills only EMPTY columns); accepted as a bounded 2-day tail rather than editing queued public content. 2026-09-24 10:4xZ ops-triage: THE PIVOT'S OWN EVIDENCE WAS UNWATCHED -- now guarded, and verified against real data. The whole discovery pivot ('non-follower reach is a measured zero, so no content lever can move followers') rests on growth_snapshots.non_follower_reach, and that path is BEST-EFFORT BY DESIGN: MetricsCollector swallows a failed insights call, logs one warning and stores NULL, so the measurement can stop running with no error anywhere. check_insights_stale does NOT cover it (posts.insights_updated_at is a different endpoint and producer), latest_discovery_attribution() returns the newest NON-NULL row with NO age bound -- so this item's own evidence text would keep asserting non-follower=0 from a row that no longer describes the present -- and the client's own note says a breakdown that never reconciles with the account total 'is how a silently broken breakdown would show itself', yet no check compared the parts to the whole. FIXED in the repo: new check_discovery_attribution + pure attribution_verdict, firing on (a) newest attribution older than 6h (snapshots are hourly), (b) reach answered WITHOUT a follow_type breakdown = unmeasured, never zero, (c) follower+non-follower != reach_total. Staleness is judged FIRST so an old row cannot be reported as live. VERIFIED: selftest 646/0 (was 636; 10 new cases incl. never-measured-is-not-a-defect, right-at-bound, stale-beats-content); checks-audit 57 checks 0 raised 0 unreadable (was 56); and the check is not vacuous -- the live row (nf|fl|total = 0|5|5) reads quiet while the SAME row aged 7h returns warn and fl+1 returns the non-reconcile warn. DECISION, unchanged and now guarded: the arm stays SEQUENCED after the 2026-10-05 13:00Z read (the only missing piece is the rail wiring; a reel publishes with no photo, so it stays out of GateRead#cohort_size by construction), its success metric is non_follower_reach>0 -- the exact number this check now proves is still being taken -- and no levers, renders, GPU claims or posts were touched by this pass. Item stays open as the gate's continuously-tracked acceptance counter; self-closes on the first engaged published post.

Measured read-only against the Graph API this pass: (1) the account node reports media_count=224 against 149 posts this app published with a provider id (a platform inventory LARGER than ours, so nothing has been lost); (2) the newest 10 published posts are all still retrievable (10/10, not_retrievable=0) and the platform's own like_count/comments_count agree with our columns exactly (0/0 on every one, matching db_likes/db_comments 0). VERDICT: (b) is refuted -- the inventory is intact and the counters are real -- so the zero is a genuine DISTRIBUTION outcome, which is what the pre-registered pivot candidate names. The hand-run check is now MACHINERY rather than a story: growth_snapshots.media_count is collected on every hourly snapshot (same account-node call as followers_count, no extra round trip, NULL when unanswered so an unmeasured inventory can never read as 'nothing was removed') and a new probe check platform-media-removed fires on a strict decrease below the recorded peak -- publishing can only INCREASE media_count, so a decrease is removal stated by the platform rather than inferred from our bookkeeping.
